doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Racial mixing in the studios
summary: Raph says rock and roll dates were half black and half white with no real line of distinction.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What was the racial scene like in the studio work? And did it change?

Rock & roll was half black half white, for openers. I remember doing many dates where I might have been the only white musician and doing dates where there were a few blacks. It’s hard to — there was never really a line of distinction. I think it just flowed. You went one way or the other, it didn’t matter. Your friends were of all colors and it was just part of the way the world is.
